name: Silhouette Guest Drop
why_it_works: A shadow plus two clues turns an announcement into a guessing game, and guesses go in the comments. Every wrong guess is engagement, and the people who guessed right feel smart and share it.

hook.pattern: Show a backlit silhouette and ask 'Who's on {{show_name}} next?' with the clue count on screen.
examples: Two clues. Guess who's on {{show_name}} next.
This shadow has a story you haven't heard.
Our next guest has never told this story on camera.

variables.name: show_name
variables.description: Podcast, team, channel or event name

variables.name: guest_role
variables.description: What the guest is known for, no name
variables.example: the trainer behind three regional champions

variables.name: clue_two
variables.example: never gave a long interview until now

variables.name: guest_name
variables.description: The guest's name, revealed last (with their consent)

visual.prompt: Vertical 9:16 photo of a person in full silhouette against a bright backlit studio wall, haze in the air, no facial features visible, microphone stand in foreground
Same silhouette from a slightly lower angle, a single prop hinting at the guest's world, rim light only, vertical 9:16
Tight shot of the silhouette's hands on a desk with a mic, backlight, haze, vertical 9:16
Studio front lights fade up on the guest seated at a mic, revealing their face, slow push-in, warm key light, vertical 9:16; use the guest's own approved photo as the start frame

cta: Comment your guess, then catch {{guest_name}} on {{show_name}} {{air_date}}.

craft.notes: Clues should go from vague to specific, and the second clue should make a few viewers certain. Post the reel a day early and pin the first correct comment so the guessing keeps going.

do_not: Generate a face for a real guest; use their own approved photo or footage for the reveal frame
Tease a guest who has not agreed to the announcement
Make clues so obscure no one can guess; zero right answers kills the comments
